Compute the site frequency spectrum of each population

Source: R/pop_sfs.R
pop_sfs.Rd

Compute the one-dimensional site frequency spectrum (SFS) of each population, i.e. the number of loci with 0, 1, 2, ... copies of the derived (or minor) allele. Missing genotypes are dealt with as in easySFS (which relies on dadi), so that the spectra can be used for demographic inference with dadi, moments or fastsimcoal2. See pairwise_pop_sfs() for the joint spectra of pairs of populations, and nwise_pop_sfs() for the joint spectrum of all populations.

Usage

pop_sfs(.x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tbl_df'
pop_sfs(
  .x,
  n_proj = NULL,
  folded = TRUE,
  ancestral = NULL,
  type = c("tidy", "array"),
  n_cores = bigstatsr::nb_cores(),
  block_size = bigstatsr::block_size(nrow(.x), 1),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'vctrs_bigSNP'
pop_sfs(
  .x,
  n_proj = NULL,
  folded = TRUE,
  ancestral = NULL,
  type = c("tidy", "array"),
  n_cores = bigstatsr::nb_cores(),
  block_size = bigstatsr::block_size(length(.x), 1),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'grouped_gen_tbl'
pop_sfs(
  .x,
  n_proj = NULL,
  folded = TRUE,
  ancestral = NULL,
  type = c("tidy", "array"),
  n_cores = bigstatsr::nb_cores(),
  block_size = bigstatsr::block_size(nrow(.x), 1),
  ...
)

Arguments

.x

a gen_tibble (grouped by population, or ungrouped to compute a single spectrum for all individuals), or a vector of class vctrs_bigSNP (usually the genotypes column of a gen_tibble).

...

other arguments passed to specific methods, currently unused.

n_proj

the number of allele copies to project each population to: either a single value used for all populations, a vector with one value per population (in the order of the groups), or a vector named with the group labels. If NULL (the default), each population is projected to the number of allele copies that maximises its number of segregating sites (see pop_sfs_preview()).

folded

boolean, whether to fold the spectrum (the default, as the ancestral allele is not usually known). If FALSE, the spectrum is polarised with ancestral.

ancestral

the ancestral allele of each locus, used to polarise unfolded spectra: either the name of a column of the loci table (see show_loci()), or a character vector with one allele per locus (in the order of the loci table). Loci whose ancestral allele is missing (NA) or is neither of their alleles are dropped. If NULL (the default), the reference allele is taken to be ancestral, as in easySFS. Ignored, with a warning, for folded spectra.

type

the type of object to return, either "tidy" (the default) or "array".

n_cores

number of cores to be used, it defaults to bigstatsr::nb_cores()

block_size

maximum number of loci read at once.

Value

If type = "tidy", a tibble with one row per cell of the spectrum of each population, with the columns:

  • group (or one column per grouping variable, if the data are grouped by more than one variable), absent for ungrouped data;

  • allele_count: the number of copies of the derived allele (for an unfolded spectrum: the alternate allele, unless the loci are polarised with ancestral) or of the minor allele (for a folded spectrum);

  • n_sites: the (projected) number of sites;

  • masked: whether the cell is masked (see details).

The projection of each population is stored in the attribute n_proj. The tibble has class pop_sfs_tbl, and can be plotted with autoplot(). If type = "array", a list of sfs objects (one per population, named by the group labels), or a single sfs object for ungrouped data. An sfs object is an array of the numbers of sites, with attributes giving its mask, the population labels (pop_ids), n_proj, whether it is folded, and the number of loci used (n_loci), dropped for lack of called allele copies (n_loci_dropped), and dropped because their ancestral allele is unknown (n_loci_unpolarised, only with ancestral). Use tidy() to turn it into a tibble.

Details

Missing data. Because of missing genotypes, the number of allele copies called at a locus varies from locus to locus. Each population is therefore projected down to a fixed number of allele copies, n_proj (Marth et al. 2004; Gutenkunst et al. 2009): a locus with \(n\) called allele copies, \(k\) of which are derived, contributes to cell \(j\) of the spectrum the hypergeometric probability of drawing \(j\) derived copies when sampling n_proj of its \(n\) copies without replacement. Loci with fewer than n_proj called copies are dropped. Each locus is thus spread over several cells, and the spectrum contains fractional numbers of sites. This is the approach of easySFS (with the -a option, i.e. using all loci).

Choosing the projection. Projecting to more allele copies gives more resolution (more segregating sites, especially rare variants), but drops more loci with missing data. Following the advice of the dadi manual and easySFS, use pop_sfs_preview() to compute the number of segregating sites for each possible projection, and choose a value that keeps most segregating sites. If n_proj is not given, each population is projected to the number of allele copies that maximises its number of segregating sites (the best projection in pop_sfs_preview()).

Folding and polarisation. Unless folded = FALSE, the spectrum is folded (i.e. it counts copies of the minor allele), as the ancestral allele is not usually known. An unfolded spectrum counts copies of the derived allele. By default (ancestral = NULL), the reference allele is taken to be ancestral, as in easySFS, so that the spectrum counts copies of the alternate allele: this is only meaningful if the alleles of the gen_tibble are polarised (note that some operations, such as merging datasets with rbind(), can swap the reference and alternate alleles). Otherwise, ancestral gives the ancestral allele of each locus (e.g. from an outgroup, or the AA field of a vcf), either as a column of the loci table or as a vector: loci whose ancestral allele is the alternate allele are polarised (copies of the reference allele are counted), and loci whose ancestral allele is missing (NA) or is neither of their two alleles are dropped, as in dadi. Alleles are compared ignoring case. Polarisation does not change a folded spectrum, so ancestral is ignored (with a warning) when folded = TRUE.

Masked cells. As in dadi, the corners of the spectrum (sites monomorphic in the projected sample) are masked, and so are the cells that were folded out in a folded spectrum. They are reported in the masked column (or the mask attribute), but keep their values.

Each spectrum only uses the loci that have enough called allele copies in its own populations. Diploid, polyploid, mixed-ploidy and pseudohaploid data are supported: each individual contributes as many allele copies as its ploidy (one for pseudohaploids). The spectrum is computed from the genotypes currently in use: if the gen_tibble uses imputed genotypes (see gt_set_imputed()), these are treated as called genotypes, so you will usually want to use gt_set_imputed(x, FALSE) first.

Note that easySFS samples a single SNP per CHROM (i.e. per RAD locus) by default; to do the same, thin the loci (e.g. with select_loci()) before computing the spectra.

References

Marth GT, Czabarka E, Murvai J, Sherry ST (2004) The allele frequency spectrum in genome-wide human variation data reveals signals of differential demographic history in three large world populations. Genetics 166: 351-372.

Gutenkunst RN, Hernandez RD, Williamson SH, Bustamante CD (2009) Inferring the joint demographic history of multiple populations from multidimensional SNP frequency data. PLoS Genetics 5: e1000695.

Overcast I. easySFS. https://github.com/isaacovercast/easySFS

Examples

example_gt <- load_example_gt("grouped_gen_tbl")

# Preview the number of segregating sites for each projection
example_gt %>% pop_sfs_preview()
#> # A tibble: 11 × 5
#>    group n_proj n_seg_sites n_loci best 
#>    <chr>  <int>       <dbl>  <dbl> <lgl>
#>  1 pop1       2        2.67      6 FALSE
#>  2 pop1       3        4         6 FALSE
#>  3 pop1       4        4.53      6 TRUE 
#>  4 pop1       5        3.83      5 FALSE
#>  5 pop1       6        4         5 FALSE
#>  6 pop2       2        2         6 FALSE
#>  7 pop2       3        3         5 FALSE
#>  8 pop2       4        4         5 TRUE 
#>  9 pop3       2        3         6 TRUE 
#> 10 pop3       3        1.5       4 FALSE
#> 11 pop3       4        2         4 FALSE

# Compute the folded spectra, projecting each population to 2 copies
example_gt %>% pop_sfs(n_proj = 2)
#> # A tibble: 9 × 4
#>   group allele_count n_sites masked
#>   <chr>        <int>   <dbl> <lgl> 
#> 1 pop1             0    3.33 TRUE  
#> 2 pop1             1    2.67 FALSE 
#> 3 pop1             2    0    TRUE  
#> 4 pop2             0    4    TRUE  
#> 5 pop2             1    2    FALSE 
#> 6 pop2             2    0    TRUE  
#> 7 pop3             0    3    TRUE  
#> 8 pop3             1    3    FALSE 
#> 9 pop3             2    0    TRUE  

# Project each population to a different number of copies
example_gt %>% pop_sfs(n_proj = c(pop1 = 4, pop2 = 2, pop3 = 2))
#> # A tibble: 11 × 4
#>    group allele_count n_sites masked
#>    <chr>        <int>   <dbl> <lgl> 
#>  1 pop1             0    1.47 TRUE  
#>  2 pop1             1    2.13 FALSE 
#>  3 pop1             2    2.4  FALSE 
#>  4 pop1             3    0    TRUE  
#>  5 pop1             4    0    TRUE  
#>  6 pop2             0    4    TRUE  
#>  7 pop2             1    2    FALSE 
#>  8 pop2             2    0    TRUE  
#>  9 pop3             0    3    TRUE  
#> 10 pop3             1    3    FALSE 
#> 11 pop3             2    0    TRUE  

# Unfolded spectra, as arrays
example_gt %>% pop_sfs(n_proj = 2, folded = FALSE, type = "array")
#> $pop1
#> # An unfolded site frequency spectrum of 1 population
#> # Allele copies: pop1 = 2
#> # Loci used: 6 (dropped for missing data: 0)
#> pop1
#>        0        1        2 
#> 2.166667 2.666667 1.166667 
#> 
#> $pop2
#> # An unfolded site frequency spectrum of 1 population
#> # Allele copies: pop2 = 2
#> # Loci used: 6 (dropped for missing data: 0)
#> pop2
#>   0   1   2 
#> 3.5 2.0 0.5 
#> 
#> $pop3
#> # An unfolded site frequency spectrum of 1 population
#> # Allele copies: pop3 = 2
#> # Loci used: 6 (dropped for missing data: 0)
#> pop3
#> 0 1 2 
#> 3 3 0 
#> 

# Unfolded spectra, polarised with the ancestral allele of each locus (the
# locus with an unknown ancestral allele is dropped)
show_loci(example_gt)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 7
#>   big_index name  chromosome position genetic_dist allele_ref allele_alt
#>       <int> <chr> <fct>         <int>        <dbl> <chr>      <chr>     
#> 1         1 rs1   chr1              3            0 A          T         
#> 2         2 rs2   chr1              5            0 T          C         
#> 3         3 rs3   chr1             65            0 C          NA        
#> 4         4 rs4   chr1            343            0 G          C         
#> 5         5 rs5   chr2             23            0 C          G         
#> 6         6 rs6   chr2            456            0 T          A         
example_gt %>%
  pop_sfs(
    n_proj = 2, folded = FALSE,
    ancestral = c("T", "C", "C", "G", NA, "T")
  )
#> # A tibble: 9 × 4
#>   group allele_count n_sites masked
#>   <chr>        <int>   <dbl> <lgl> 
#> 1 pop1             0    2.63 TRUE  
#> 2 pop1             1    2.07 FALSE 
#> 3 pop1             2    0.3  TRUE  
#> 4 pop2             0    2.5  TRUE  
#> 5 pop2             1    1.5  FALSE 
#> 6 pop2             2    1    TRUE  
#> 7 pop3             0    1.5  TRUE  
#> 8 pop3             1    2    FALSE 
#> 9 pop3             2    1.5  TRUE
